A skip on the direct edge 0->3 already gives a decent, well-trained parent, so the conv upgrade on edge 4 has less to add.

Adding a skip where the edge was absent is a large gain, while replacing an existing conv or pool with skip is neutral or negative.
Parents with a pooling edge upstream are lower quality with more headroom, so the downstream conv upgrade gains more.
Parents with a pool on edge 4 are weak and variable, so a skip on edge 0 recovers more than when edge 4 is already conv.
Weak parents with a pooled output edge gain more from a skip into node 2, while parents with conv on edge 5 are near saturation.
Pruning the cross edge costs less when a strong conv already feeds node 2 in parallel, because the removed contribution is largely redundant.
